newsitem.title: USA: Digital Q3 sales fall, sees Q4 loss.
newsitem.headline: Digital Q3 sales fall, sees Q4 loss.

text.p: Digital Communications Technology Corp reported Wednesday lower third quarter sales and said continuing slow sales would likely result in a fourth quarter loss.
The company reported revenues of $3,981,243 for the quarter to March 31, down from $5,929,998 in the 1996 quarter.
Net loss for the quarter was $796,532, or $0.11 per share, versus net income of $348,050, or $0.06 per share, for the comparable period last year.
First Call estimates for the company were not immediately available.
"The low level of sales for the quarter ending March 31, 1997 were totally unexpected," a company statement said.

Digital said total sales for the month of March -- $843,000 -- was the lowest monthly sales it experienced in several years. In the same month last year, the company said, total sales were $2.2 million.
"The slow trend has continued into the fourth quarter and the company expects to report additional losses for the quarter ending June 30, 1997," the statement said.
The company said, however, that it has not lost any of its customer base and it is implementing measures that should return it to profitability in fiscal 1998.
The company gave no indication of when it would release fourth quarter results and calls to its Dallas headquarters were not immediately answered.
